summary: Extends the IPsec Domain of Interpretation for ISAKMP so that two ends can negotiate whether to use traditional 32-bit sequence numbers or extended 64-bit sequence numbers to detect replays in AH or ESP. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Packets are numbered to catch copies. This memo lets the two sides agree to use longer numbers, so the counter does not run out.

questions: what is ipsec extended sequence number
how do ipsec peers negotiate 64-bit sequence numbers
subtitle: How two IPsec peers agree, during ISAKMP/IKE negotiation, to use 64-bit extended sequence numbers.

tldr.problem: AH and ESP use a sequence number to detect replay, and 32-bit numbers can run out when large volumes of data flow at high speed over one security association.
tldr.mechanism: The IPsec DOI for ISAKMP gets a new Basic SA attribute, Extended (64-bit) Sequence Number, type value 11, with class value 1 meaning 64-bit sequence numbers.
tldr.outcome: Peers can negotiate 32-bit or 64-bit numbers, and setup is aborted when an unsupported value arrives. Pick a cipher mode that is safe for very large data volumes.

today: RFC 4304 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is an addendum to the DOI in RFC 2407.

sections.title: Why Extended Sequence Numbers
sections.content:
The specifications for the IP Authentication Header (AH) and Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) describe an option for extended (64-bit) sequence numbers. It permits very large volumes of data at high speeds over one security association without rekeying to avoid exhausting the sequence number space.

RFC 4304 adds what the IPsec Domain of Interpretation (DOI) for ISAKMP needs in order to negotiate that option.
sections.eli5: A counter that is too short wraps around. A longer counter lasts much longer, and this memo lets both sides agree to use it.

sections.title: The ESN Attribute
sections.content:
The new SA attribute is used in Phase II of an IKE negotiation. It is called Extended (64-bit) Sequence Number, has attribute value 11 and is of type Basic (B). Basic attributes MUST NOT be encoded as variable.

Its class values are 0 (RESERVED) and 1 (64-bit Sequence Number). The class specifies that the security association will use 64-bit sequence numbers.
sections.eli5: It is one extra checkbox on the negotiation form: 'use the long counter, yes'.

sections.title: Attribute Negotiation
sections.content: If an implementation receives a defined IPsec DOI attribute or value it does not support, it SHOULD send ATTRIBUTES-NOT-SUPPORT and MUST abort the security association setup. If it receives any value other than the one for 64-bit sequence numbers, setup MUST be aborted.
sections.eli5: If one side does not understand the request, it says so and the two sides do not set up the connection.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Adding the ESN attribute does not change the underlying security characteristics of IKE. With ESP, it is important to use an encryption mode that is secure when very large volumes of data are encrypted under one key. For example, DES in CBC mode would NOT be suitable, because no more than 2^32 blocks should be encrypted under a single DES key in that mode.

The integrity algorithm should also be secure relative to the number of packets protected. The SA lifetime may be set to limit the data protected by a single key before reaching the 2^64 packet limit of the ESN.
sections.eli5: Using one key for a huge amount of data can wear it out, so choose strong locks and change keys sometimes.

items.label: 64-bit Sequence Number
items.desc: The SA will use 64-bit sequence numbers.
